title: OperationReceipt
description: The per-step receipt of the endpoint-originated validation journey (ADR-068 §30, §4.8). It binds the step's verdict to the EXACT ORIGIN of its inputs: operator, implementation, endpoint, resolved host, fetched-at, HTTP status, content type/length, ETag, hash, signature status and engine version. Protocol fetches are counted as `protocol_fetch_count`, never as `external_model_calls`; in validation mode `qwen_calls` and `external_model_calls` are always 0 (Rust decides, the model never decides). A receipt is NOT a certificate. A receipt seals a TERMINAL step state — `result.status` is one of {VERIFIED,PENDING,FAILED,BLOCKED}; the transient `RUNNING` state (ADR-076 §D-076-04) is a live-execution state and is never sealed into a receipt. Documentary/reference contract; introduces no new financial invariant.
_authority: ADR-068 (§4.8 receipts, §30 OperationReceipt), ADR-076 (§D-076-07 receipt §4 field set; §D-076-08 durable append-only persistence), ADR-077 (profile applicability model — the `applicability` field + NOT_EVALUATED terminal for a NOT_APPLICABLE step), ADR-037 (Rust-first engines), ADR-066 (closed certification-state machine)
_boundary: A receipt records what was fetched and what Rust decided. It never certifies, admits, authorises, or moves funds. It carries NO free BanzAI/model text (ADR-076 §D-076-08).
_canonical_field_equivalence: ADR-076 §4 canonical names map onto this schema's origin-bound §30 names as: execution_id ≡ operation_id, engine_name ≡ engine, receipt_reference ≡ audit_ref, input_artifact_digests ⊇ input_hash (the scalar input_hash stays; input_artifact_digests adds the structured per-artefact breakdown). New durable artefacts (the Postgres receipt store, the journey state-machine contract) use the canonical §4 names; this receipt keeps its established §30 names plus the new §4 behavioural fields below.

operation_id.description: Unique id of this step operation (e.g. 'op-<uuid>').

request_id.description: Id shared by all steps of the same journey/step request.

applicability.description: ADR-077: the step's applicability to the target's declared conformance profile, ORTHOGONAL to result.status. REQUIRED = in scope and must be evaluated; OPTIONAL = in scope, non-blocking; NOT_APPLICABLE = out of scope for the profile (e.g. L2 interoperability / L3 federation for an L0 implementation) — such a step is never fetched or engine-evaluated (result.status = NOT_EVALUATED), never a technical failure, and never contributes to readiness. Rust decides the map (banza-target-registry). Always emitted by the runtime as of ADR-077.

canonical_origin.description: The implementation's canonical origin the artifacts were fetched from.

endpoint.description: The primary endpoint URL fetched for this step.

resolved_host.description: The host the fetcher pinned to and connected to.

fetched_at.description: When the primary artifact was fetched (RFC3339 UTC).

http_status.description: HTTP status of the primary fetch.

input_hash.description: Hash of the engine input assembled from fetched content (e.g. 'sha256:...').

signature_status.description: Signature evaluation status for the key/trust steps; 'not_applicable' otherwise.

engine.description: The Rust decision engine that produced the verdict for this step.

result.description: The engine verdict for this step (status + engine output/reason). Decided in Rust.

status.description: Canonical step status decided by Rust. NOT_EVALUATED is the terminal of a NOT_APPLICABLE step (ADR-077) — out of scope for the profile, never fetched or evaluated.

reason_codes.description: Typed reason codes (verdict reasons and/or fetcher reason codes on BLOCKED).

evidence_refs.description: Origin-bound references, each an endpoint URL plus the content hash fetched from it.

protocol_fetch_count.description: Number of successful protocol fetches for this step. Never counted as external model calls.

audit_ref.description: Correlation reference joining the request id and the fetcher audit id (≡ ADR-076 receipt_reference).

started_at.description: ADR-076 §4: when the step began executing (RFC3339 UTC). Optional in v1.1; promoted to required once the runtime emits it.

completed_at.description: ADR-076 §4: when the step reached its terminal state (RFC3339 UTC).

retryable.description: ADR-076 §4: whether this step may be safely re-run (a fetch/transient failure is retryable; a decided FAILED verdict is not).

blocked_by.description: ADR-076 §4: the upstream step ids whose non-VERIFIED state blocks this step. Empty when nothing blocks it.

input_artifact_digests.description: ADR-076 §4: structured per-artefact digest map (superset of the scalar input_hash). Each key is an artefact role; each value binds the endpoint fetched to its content digest.

endpoint.description: The endpoint URL the artefact was fetched from.

sha256.description: Content digest 'sha256:...' of the fetched artefact.
